newsitem.title: USA: USWC products firm on Calif. hydrocrackers snags.
newsitem.headline: USWC products firm on Calif. hydrocrackers snags.

text.p: U.S. West Coast diesel prices firmed early Thursday, brokers said, lifted by ongoing problems at hydrocrackers operated by ARCO and Tosco in California.
Workers shut the 4,000 barrel-per-day ARCO hydrocracker on Monday to repair a leak, while the larger Tosco unit caught fire last week, killing one worker and injuring others.

ARCO has raised racks about eight cents the last two days in order to discourage buying until it can bring the unit on line Friday. The company bought about 60,000 barrels of diesel to cover the unit's lost output.
Bids for California CARB diesel rose two cents from Wednesday to 85 cents a gallon, while buyers of low sulphur grade asked for 74 cents a gallon, or 0.50 cents more than yesterday, traders said.
In gasoline markets, San Francisco conventional gasoline was flat at 76, traders said.
